ambient_env.note: Recorded before any arm was bound. The harness overwrites its own route flags; any other HIPENGINE_* value listed here was ambient for this capture and must be reviewed before the capture is compared with another run.

backend_scope.note: The registered PARO MTP strict/production plans, their route binder and the capture manifest binding exist only for this backend. A run on another backend is refused rather than reporting a manifest and route attestation that do not describe it. This is a diagnostic-scope limit, not model, quantization or runtime admission.

envelope_disagreement.note: Both envelopes are reported as observed sample comparisons and neither decides admission or a rate gate. Where the 2026-08-16 mean/tail sample exceeds a limit the binding 2.11 sample does not, 2.11 is the applicable envelope for this sparse top-k MoE model class; the legacy numbers stay reported so saved rejections remain readable.

current_sparse_moe_policy.applies_to: sparse top-k expert routing; this harness targets qwen3_5_moe_paro
current_sparse_moe_policy.binding_basis: Router-routing-scoped production KL envelope for models with sparse top-k expert routing. It is the envelope this report's observed median/p90 KL, flip-damage and top-1 comparisons are named against.

rate_gate_policy.reason: docs/EXECUTION-PROFILES.md 6.4 rule 1: top-1 agreement and the flip-damage rate are rate gates. A reduced run reports them as counts with intervals and never as a pass/fail, at any row count. This single-prompt capture is not the full protocol, so no rate gate is decided here - including one whose interval lies entirely on the failing side of its limit.

legacy_mean_tail_kl_envelope.binding_basis: Superseded for this model class by 2.11. Thresholds and observed comparisons are reported unchanged so saved historical rejections keep their recorded meaning; they do not decide admission here. For a model class without sparse top-k expert routing these thresholds remain the binding 6.1 envelope.

legacy_review_manifest.note: Pre-2026-10-24 hand-built reporting manifest. Its b1_graph_off_fixed_chain scope is not a registered selection, and its uncertified/unselected labels were stale. Kept only so saved v3 capture hashes remain identifiable.

covers: B1 fixed-chain strict-versus-candidate target verifier full-vocabulary logits on a strict-owned teacher-forced schedule
host candidate handoff and synchronized post-commit state
does_not_cover: the public adapter's route selection, rollback and asynchronous publication
B2/B3 draft depths, including the depth-2 to depth-1 output-tail transition
isolated kernel attribution: candidate recurrent/KV state is carried, not reset to strict values per cycle
serial-AR equality: the strict teacher here is a B1 verifier trajectory
any admission or rate-gate decision: a single-prompt screen issues none at any row count
full_qualification_requires: task non-inferiority on the applicable prompt suite and heldouts under a predeclared paired criterion
three bit-identical fixed-seed repeats of the same manifest and execution schedule
the full protocol across the prompt suite, whose top-1 and flip-damage rate gates a single-prompt capture cannot decide (EXECUTION-PROFILES 6.4)
B2/B3 captures through the public adapter

route_attestation.note: Agreement means the harness writes the same selectors the registered binder writes. It does not establish that every selector has a live consumer in the runtime, nor that ambient selectors outside this list are inert; ambient HIPENGINE_* values are recorded separately.

runner_reported_metadata.note: The runner defaults finite_logits and gpu_accept_match_cpu on its trusted-GPU path without reading every full-vocabulary logit or the CPU accept oracle. They are recorded here, not used as evidence; this harness's own finiteness check reads the captured logits.

sample_scope.continuous_gate_policy: docs/EXECUTION-PROFILES.md 6.4 rules 1-3: median and p90 KL are reported as observed sample values. Reading a sample against a full-protocol limit needs a control scope with a known full-gate verdict in the same batch and a screen-to-full ratio interval; a one-prompt capture has neither, so no continuous gate is decided and no ratio correction is applied.
sample_scope.rate_gate_policy: docs/EXECUTION-PROFILES.md 6.4 rule 1: top-1 agreement and the flip-damage rate are rate gates. A reduced run reports them as counts with intervals and never as a pass/fail, at any row count. This single-prompt capture is not the full protocol, so no rate gate is decided here - including one whose interval lies entirely on the failing side of its limit.
sample_scope.reason: The canonical full protocol is 12 cases x 129 transitions across the prompt suite (1548 rows), not a row count from one prompt. A single-prompt B1 capture is a screen at every row count, so it never becomes the full protocol by accumulating rows.

scope_failures_note: Binding scopes whose sample top-1 missed the 6.1 floor. On a single-prompt capture this is an observation, not a rate-gate decision; the sibling aggregation script consumes it across prompts.
teacher_forcing: strict-owned proposals, commit rows, tokens, positions, and contexts

capture_provenance.scope: 32 B1 teacher-forced rows from one raw Japanese prompt; no full policy decision
